title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
summary: The Benchmark Nifty saw a 0.7% rise, signaling a continuation of its positive trajectory. Market analysts foresee a period of consolidation ahead, with a gradual uptick on the horizon. The key resistance levels for the index are 22,650 and 22,800, while support is noted at 22,500. Additionally, foreign portfolio investors recorded net buys of Rs 1,165 crore, contrasting with a trend of domestic outflows.

title: Stocks in news: Vedanta, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, HFCL, IREDA, Zen Tech and Oil India
summary: Indian equities turned around as information technology stocks attracted sustained buying interest. Strong quarterly earnings reports enhanced investor confidence in the market, with the Nifty 50 index achieving a closing point of 23,146, representing a 0.65% rise. Prominent companies like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank shared their quarterly outcomes, showcasing improved asset quality. Investors are anticipated to keep an eye on upcoming corporate announcements which may guide market trends.

title: Nifty rally faces crucial test at key resistance levels: Analysts
summary: Nifty gained 3% last week, forming a higher-top and higher-bottom structure, indicating bullish sentiment. Analysts suggest it must breach key resistance levels for more substantial gains ahead. Meanwhile, Bank Nifty is approaching significant resistance, which may hinder further upside potential shortly. Key stocks like Coforge, Kotak Bank, and Indian Hotels present buying opportunities based on technical analysis.

title: Public sector banks' Rs 7.8 lakh core corporate loan pipeline signals capex revival
summary: Public sector banks have revealed a corporate loan pipeline of approximately ₹7.8 lakh crore signaling increased credit demand. Companies are stepping up their investment, particularly in sectors like renewable energy and semiconductor manufacturing. Banks report varied corporate credit growth, with some institutions witnessing over 50% increase year-on-year. Mid-sized and large companies are leading the way in capital expenditure, while smaller suppliers are also finding opportunities.

title: Banks also count cost of insurance payout curbs
summary: Central Bank of India anticipates a 33% decline in bancassurance fees due to proposed regulations. Canara Bank expects a ₹145-crore hit to its fee income from similar changes. Axis Bank aims to mitigate losses through increased sales volumes and alternative income sources. HDFC Bank has not yet assessed the potential impact of the new rules.

title: Tata Sons reviews AoA to meet Sebi listing norms
summary: Tata Sons is reviewing its Articles of Association to comply with Sebi listing regulations, which may impact the influence of Tata Trusts on board appointments. This scrutiny follows the RBI's rejection of Tata Sons' application to relinquish its core investment company registration, necessitating compliance with strict governance standards for listed entities.

title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
summary: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.

title: Veteran SIP investors not deterred by stagnant market: Kotak Mahindra's's Harsha Upadhyaya
summary: Even after two years of range-bound markets and rising rates, seasoned SIP investors are staying the course. Harsha Upadhyaya, chief investment officer at Kotak Mahindra AMC, explains why long-term savers remain resilient, and how RBI's hawkish turn could reshape investor behaviour.
